v.why: Replacing a parameter-free skip with a 3x3 conv gives a much larger gain than replacing other ops, as in the all-skip parent (+43).
Upgrading a skip edge to a conv gives large gains (+34 to +37 in the weak parents) versus near zero when the edge already holds a conv.
Skip-to-3x3 on edge 2 yields +35 in the all-skip parent but only small gains elsewhere.
Replacing the direct input-output skip with a conv helps most when the network has no other conv capacity (+36 in the all-skip parent).
Skip-to-3x3 on edge 4 gives large gains in the all-skip parent (+35) and moderate gains in the other skip cases.
Edge 5 feeds the output, so replacing its skip with a conv gives a very large gain in the all-skip parent (+45).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 2 with a skip consistently reduces accuracy (-0.5 to -6), while replacing other ops changes it little.
Replacing the output edge's 3x3 conv with pooling costs accuracy on all three datasets (rows 95 and 100).
Removing a 3x3 conv edge hurts (-0.5 to -15), whereas removing a weak skip or pool edge can help.
Removing a skip on edge 4 helped greatly in the all-skip parent (+27 on CIFAR-10), unlike removing a conv edge.

raw:
These hypotheses come from patterns in the 100 experiments, plus prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201. The strongest evidence is that upgrading an edge to nor_conv_3x3 gains far more when that edge was skip_connect, as in the all-skip parents (+30 to +45 on CIFAR). I did not run any further experiments or checks.

The "lower" hypotheses are weaker, especially the `nor_conv_3x3`-replacement ones, which rest on a few small, consistently negative rows. The weakest are edge 3 → `nor_conv_3x3` (rows 36 and 39 are mixed) and edge 4 → `none` when edge 4 is `skip_connect` (row 87 is near zero).
